sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In the spring of 1985, Bill Mora was wrapping up his high school education
sentences.zh: 1985年春天，比尔·莫拉即将结束他的高中学业，

sentences.en: and getting ready to move to Poughkeepsie, New York.
sentences.zh: 并准备搬到纽约州波基普西。

sentences.en: Come fall, he'd be starting his freshman year at Vassar College.
sentences.zh: 到了秋天，他将在瓦萨学院开始他的大一生活。

sentences.en: Like many incoming college students, Bill was concerned about how he would pay for his education.
sentences.zh: 和许多刚入学的大学生一样，比尔很关心自己该如何支付学费。

sentences.en: My financial aid package in my freshman year was basically a combination of student loans and work-study.
sentences.zh: 我大一时的财务资助组合基本上是由学生贷款和勤工俭学构成的。

sentences.en: But at the end of Bill's sophomore year, he received an unexpected letter in the mail.
sentences.zh: 但在比尔大二结束时，他意外收到了一封信。

sentences.en: I get this letter congratulating me for receiving something called the Hager Scholars Award.
sentences.zh: 我收到了这封信，祝贺我获得了某种名为“黑格学者奖”的奖项。

sentences.en: And the letter explained that the award would take the place in my financial aid package of my student loan.
sentences.zh: 信中解释说，这个奖项将在我的资助方案中替代我的学生贷款。

sentences.en: And here's what it said.
sentences.zh: 信上是这么写的：

sentences.en: This is an interest-free loan with a moral obligation to repay.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔免息贷款，但带有一种偿还的道德义务。

sentences.en: So, you know, at the time I was like, what is that?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，当时我就在想，那是什么？

sentences.en: I don't know what this is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是什么。

sentences.en: Sometimes I show it to my mom.
sentences.zh: 有时我把它拿给我妈妈看。

sentences.en: She's like, yeah, it's just a grant.
sentences.zh: 她说，嗨，这只是一笔补助金。

sentences.en: You're fine.
sentences.zh: 没事的。

sentences.en: Just take the money.
sentences.zh: 把钱收下就行了。

sentences.en: But, you know, I graduated.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我毕业了。

sentences.en: I went to graduate school.
sentences.zh: 我去了研究生院。

sentences.en: I became a professor.
sentences.zh: 我成了一名教授。

sentences.en: I paid off all my actual student loans.
sentences.zh: 我还清了所有真正的学生贷款。

sentences.en: And when I had done so, I thought to myself, oh, wait, I'm not done yet.
sentences.zh: 当我把这些都还清时，我心想，哦，等等，我还没完呢。

sentences.en: There's that Hager Award.
sentences.zh: 还有那个黑格奖。

sentences.en: And so I, like, you know, go online and look it up.
sentences.zh: 所以我就，你知道的，上网查了一下。

sentences.en: And I'm like, yeah, there it is.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，好吧，它就在那儿。

sentences.en: Like, I have a moral obligation to repay.
sentences.zh: 就像，我有一种偿还的道德义务。

sentences.en: I better start repaying this thing.
sentences.zh: 我最好开始把这笔钱还了。

sentences.en: And that letter, that line, that thing about how, you know, you have a moral obligation, it caught me.
sentences.zh: 而那封信、那句话、关于你有一种道德义务的说法，击中了我。

sentences.en: It grabbed me and pulled me right in.
sentences.zh: 它一把抓住我，把我深深地拉了进去。

sentences.en: The award made explicit something that's often overlooked in the way we think about money.
sentences.zh: 这个奖项明确表达了一点：我们在看待金钱时常常忽视了这一点。

sentences.en: At its core, money is about human relationships.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，金钱关乎人际关系。

sentences.en: And at a macro level, loans and gifts and paychecks and the dollars that come out of ATMs are clues to a culture, even the structure of a nation.
sentences.zh: 从宏观层面来看，贷款、礼物、薪水以及从自动取款机里吐出来的钞票，都是一个文化甚至是一个国家结构的线索。

sentences.en: So far in our Money 2.0 series, we've looked at the scripts we follow when it comes to money and the traps we fall into when it comes to budgets.
sentences.zh: 在我们的“金钱 2.0”系列节目中，我们已经探讨了我们在对待金钱时遵循的剧本，以及我们在面对预算时陷入的陷阱。

sentences.en: Today we ask, where does the value of money come from in the first place?
sentences.zh: 今天我们要问：金钱的价值最初究竟来自哪里？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we revisit a 2020 episode about the intangible elements of cold, hard cash.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们重温了 2020 年的一期节目，探讨冷冰冰的现金背后那些无形的元素。

sentences.en: Coins and currency are not just tokens of economic value, but markers of emotional connection and shared history.
sentences.zh: 硬币和货币不仅是经济价值的象征，也是情感联系和共同历史的标记。

sentences.en: There's a story we tell about what the world looked like before we invented money.
sentences.zh: 关于在我们发明货币之前世界是什么样子的，流传着这样一个故事。

sentences.en: It's a story built on the idea of barter.
sentences.zh: 这是一个建立在以物易物概念上的故事。

sentences.en: This is the standard story that we read in the economics textbooks and that has been handed down to us at least since the mid-19th century, if not before.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在经济学教科书里读到的标准故事，至少从19世纪中期甚至更早开始，就一直流传至今。

sentences.en: This again is anthropologist Bill Maurer, who told us the story of his moral obligation to repay that student loan.
sentences.zh: 这位再次登场的 anthropologists 比尔·毛尔，曾向我们讲述了他偿还那笔学生贷款的道德义务的故事。

sentences.en: He's now the dean of the School of Social Sciences at the University of California, Irvine, and he studies the origins and nature of money.
sentences.zh: 他现在是加州大学欧文分校社会科学学院的院长，他专门研究货币的起源和本质。

sentences.en: And it goes something like this.
sentences.zh: 事情大概是这样的：

sentences.en: In the beginning, before there was money, if I had something that you needed, I would approach you with that thing and see if you had anything that I needed.
sentences.zh: 在最初没有货币的时候，如果我有什么东西你需要，我就会带着那个东西去找你，看看你有没有我需要的东西。

sentences.en: So if you wanted some fish and you needed some acorns and I had them, I could approach you with those acorns and we could basically barter on the spot,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想要一些鱼，而你需要橡果，而我正好有，我就可以带着这些橡果去找你，我们基本上就可以当场以物易物，

sentences.en: figuring out how many acorns equals how many fish.
sentences.zh: 算清楚多少橡果等于多少鱼。

sentences.en: The problem with barter is it really does depend on us each meeting each other's needs in that moment.
sentences.zh: 以物易物的问题在于，它确实取决于我们双方在那个当下的需求恰好能对上。

sentences.en: And so the origin story of money that we have is that humans invented money essentially to be a mediator in these sorts of exchanges.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们所拥有的货币起源故事是：人类发明货币，本质上是为了在这些类型的交易中充当调解人。

sentences.en: In other words, if you, for example, had acorns, but I didn't actually want acorns.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你，比如说，有橡果，但我其实并不想要橡果。

sentences.en: I wanted pots, for example, and I wanted to trade my fish for pots and all you had to offer me was acorns, then essentially we couldn't negotiate.
sentences.zh: 比如我想要罐子，我想用我的鱼换罐子，而你唯一能提供给我的只有橡果，那么本质上我们就无法进行协商。

sentences.en: And economists sometimes have a term for this.
sentences.zh: 经济学家有时会用一个术语来形容这种情况。

sentences.en: They say that barter requires something called a double coincidence of wants.
sentences.zh: 他们说以物易物需要一种叫做“需求双重巧合”的东西。

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: The double coincidence of wants essentially means that in that moment, I've got what you need, you've got what I need.
sentences.zh: 需求双重巧合本质上意味着在那一刻，我有你需要的东西，你也有我需要的东西。

sentences.en: There's a coincidence of our needs in the instance.
sentences.zh: 我们的需求在那个瞬间刚好吻合了。

sentences.en: And that rarely happens, right?
sentences.zh: 而这种情况很少发生，对吧？

sentences.en: So the idea here is that humans wizard up this kind of third thing, money,
sentences.zh: 所以这里的观点是，人类凭空捏造出了这种第三种东西，也就是金钱，

sentences.en: this magical substance that can put all things on one scale of value and use that as sort of their measuring stick then to make these kinds of transactions.
sentences.zh: 这是一种神奇的物质，能把所有东西放在同一个价值天平上，然后把它当作一种衡量标准，以此来进行这类交易。

sentences.en: So there's a problem with the story and the problem is that it runs into some facts.
sentences.zh: 所以这个故事有个问题，问题在于它与某些事实相冲突。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you can tell me about the work that you and other anthropologists have done, for example, in the highlands of New Guinea,
sentences.zh: 我想知道您能否跟我讲讲您和其他人类学家所做的工作，比如在新几内亚高地，

sentences.en: that call into question this origin story.
sentences.zh: 这些研究对这个起源故事提出了质疑。

sentences.en: The problem is that when we look around the world and in the historical and archaeological record for instances of this kind of direct barter, unfortunately, we don't find it.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当我们环顾世界，并在历史和考古记录中寻找这种直接以物易物的实例时，遗憾的是，我们找不到。

sentences.en: What we find instead really are systems where people are taking some kind of object.
sentences.zh: 我们真正发现的，反而是人们用某种物品建立系统的现象。

sentences.en: Let's take a kind of a big shell valuable in the highlands of New Guinea and using it to mark relationships.
sentences.zh: 比方说，在新几内亚高地有一种很大的贝壳贵重物品，人们用它来标记关系。

sentences.en: They're using it to mark relationships among people, among kin, that serve as a kind of indicator of enduring obligations that people have to one another.
sentences.zh: 他们用它来标记人与人之间、亲属之间的关系，这可以作为人们之间持久义务的一种指标。

sentences.en: It's kind of like an open-ended IOU, right?
sentences.zh: 这有点像一个开放式的欠条，对吧？

sentences.en: If I give you this big shell thing, then that implies for us, but also for everyone around us, that we have a bond.
sentences.zh: 如果我把这个巨大的贝壳东西给你，这就意味着对于我们、以及对于我们周围的每个人来说，我们之间建立了一种纽带。

sentences.en: We have a relationship that will essentially allow us to have a flow of goods between each other and between our families for the rest of our lives, essentially.
sentences.zh: 我们建立了一种关系，从本质上讲，它将使我们在余生中能够在彼此之间以及我们的家庭之间实现货物流通。

sentences.en: So it's not so much that I'm giving you this shell so that you give me some pigs.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说我给你这个贝壳是为了让你给我一些猪。

sentences.en: It's I'm giving you this shell so as to say, hey, someday I'm going to need some pigs.
sentences.zh: 而是我给你这个贝壳是为了表达：嘿，总有一天我需要一些猪。

sentences.en: Some other day I might need your help in the field.
sentences.zh: 在未来的某一天，我可能需要在田里得到你的帮助。

sentences.en: Some other day you might need me to help you out with something.
sentences.zh: 在未来的某一天，你可能会需要我帮个忙。

sentences.en: This shell kind of marks that relationship.
sentences.zh: 这个贝壳在某种程度上标志着这种关系。

sentences.en: It signifies to everyone around us that we have these ties of enduring obligation and responsibility.
sentences.zh: 它向我们周围的所有人表明，我们之间有着持久义务和责任的纽带。

sentences.en: So in other words, it's not about a transaction, at least not in an immediate sense.
sentences.zh: 所以换句话说，这无关交易，至少在即时意义上不是。

sentences.en: It's about a transaction that perhaps unfolds over time, more to do with obligation.
sentences.zh: 这关乎一种可能在时间推移中展开的交易，更多的是关于义务。

sentences.en: My son is marrying your daughter.
sentences.zh: 我的儿子要娶你的女儿。

sentences.en: I'm giving you this precious necklace that I have.
sentences.zh: 我把我的传家宝项链送给你。

sentences.en: And my expectation is over the next 20 years, our families are going to help one another in all kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 我的期望是，在未来的 20 年里，我们的家族将以各种方式互相帮助。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's really a memory device to indicate an ongoing, enduring relationship, an ongoing set of obligations.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一个记忆装置，用来标示一种持续、持久的关系，以及一系列持续的义务。

sentences.en: And is some of this connected with the more basic idea, if you will, of just gift giving?
sentences.zh: 其中是否有一些与更基础的概念，也就是单纯的馈赠礼物有关？

sentences.en: When you think about gifts, part of what we're doing when I'm giving you a gift, and presumably this is true for people all over the world in different cultures,
sentences.zh: 当你想到礼物时，当我送你一件礼物时，我们所做的一部分事情（据推测世界各地不同文化的人们都是如此），

sentences.en: the gift is partly my telling you, here's something nice for you.
sentences.zh: 这份礼物一部分是在向你表达：这是送给你的好东西。

sentences.en: But it also binds us in some kind of relationship that says down the line, you know, it's not explicit,
sentences.zh: 但它也将我们绑定在某种关系中，意味着在未来某个时候，你知道，虽然不是明说的，

sentences.en: but there's some implicit understanding that you're going to do something nice for me down the road.
sentences.zh: 但有一种隐含的理解，即你在未来也会为我做一些好事。

sentences.en: This is exactly how it works, yeah.
sentences.zh: 事情正是这样的，是的。

sentences.en: And the early anthropologist Marcel Mose wrote about this quite explicitly, saying that in the gift, there's the obligation to give, there's the obligation to receive,
sentences.zh: 早期人类学家马塞尔·莫斯曾对此有过非常明确的论述，他说在礼物中，包含着赠送的义务、接受的义务，

sentences.en: but then also the obligation to reciprocate.
sentences.zh: 但随后也包含着回报的义务。

sentences.en: This obligation to reciprocate can be seen across human societies and across time.
sentences.zh: 这种回报的义务在人类社会和历史长河中随处可见。

sentences.en: Some years ago, Bill stumbled on another interesting example of this.
sentences.zh: 几年前，比尔偶然发现了另一个有趣的例子。

sentences.en: He was in Washington, D.C., visiting a colleague who worked at the Smithsonian.
sentences.zh: 他在华盛顿特区拜访了一位在史密森尼学会工作的同事。

sentences.en: She curated the museum's collections that relate to the history of money.
sentences.zh: 她负责管理博物馆中与货币历史相关的藏品。

sentences.en: Bill was with her inside a vault.
sentences.zh: 比尔和她一起在一个金库里。

sentences.en: And there's an area in the vault in a kind of long closet, and she and her interns call it Narnia because it's sort of like the wardrobe in Narnia.
sentences.zh: 金库里有一个区域，在一个类似长衣柜的地方，她和实习生们称之为“纳尼亚”，因为这有点像《纳尼亚传奇》里的衣橱。

sentences.en: You go in and it goes on and on and on forever.
sentences.zh: 你走进去，里面没完没了地延伸下去。

sentences.en: Inside this Narnia, there are boxes upon boxes of uncatalogued artifacts.
sentences.zh: 在这个“纳尼亚”里面，堆满了装有未编目文物的盒子。

sentences.en: So I was there once with her, and she said to me, do you want to go to Narnia?
sentences.zh: 所以我有一次和她一起去，她对我说，你想去纳尼亚吗？

sentences.en: And I said, sure.
sentences.zh: 我说，当然。

sentences.en: So we go in, pull out a box at random, bring it out.
sentences.zh: 于是我们走进去，随机抽出一个箱子，把它拿出来。

sentences.en: She opens the box, and there's a ton of these clay tablets covered in cuneiform.
sentences.zh: 她打开箱子，里面有大量刻有楔形文字的泥板。

sentences.en: And there was a sort of moment where both of us back away from the box, you know, and I'm like, uh-oh, don't touch anything.
sentences.zh: 当时我们俩都有那么一刻从箱子旁退了开来，你知道的，我想，哦哦，什么都别碰。

sentences.en: Don't break anything.
sentences.zh: 什么都别弄坏。

sentences.en: Don't breathe.
sentences.zh: 呼吸都放轻点。

sentences.en: The clay tablets that they pulled out of the box were used 5,000 years ago in ancient Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 他们从箱子里拿出来的那些泥板，是 5000 年前在古代美索不达米亚使用的。

sentences.en: They were used to keep records of obligations.
sentences.zh: 它们被用来记录各种义务。

sentences.en: When people lived in small groups, monitoring obligations was easy.
sentences.zh: 当人们生活在小群体中时，监督义务是很简单的。

sentences.en: I just remembered what you had said and done, and you remembered what I had said and done.
sentences.zh: 我只记得你说过的话和做过的事，你也记得我说过的话和做过的事。

sentences.en: But as human societies grew larger, people needed a way to systematically keep track of who owed what to whom.
sentences.zh: 但是随着人类社会规模的扩大，人们需要一种系统化的方法来追踪谁欠了谁什么。

sentences.en: And we just can't keep track of all of that in our heads.
sentences.zh: 我们根本无法在脑子里记住所有这些事情。

sentences.en: What emerges, essentially, are systems of public administration, where you've got centralized authorities who are responsible for organizing irrigation, organizing production,
sentences.zh: 本质上涌现出来的是公共管理系统，由集权当局负责组织灌溉、组织生产，

sentences.en: so that you can have these larger-scale settlements, who set up systems of record-keeping, in the case that you mentioned in Mesopotamia, using clay tablets,
sentences.zh: 以便形成更大规模的定居点，并建立记录保存系统——正如你提到的美索不达米亚的例子，使用泥板——

sentences.en: so that people basically know what's going on, who's doing what, who owes what to whom.
sentences.zh: 这样人们基本上就能知道发生了什么，谁在做什么，谁欠了谁什么。

sentences.en: And you don't have the situation of something like a coin circulating from hand to hand to pay your laborers, for example.
sentences.zh: 你不会看到诸如硬币在手手相传中用来支付工人工资之类的情况。

sentences.en: Instead, you have these systems of tablets that are basically receipts, keeping track of things like labor, and then promising that, you know, after a certain period,
sentences.zh: 相反，你拥有的是这些基本上是收据的泥板系统，记录着诸如劳动力之类的事情，然后承诺，你知道的，在一定时期之后，

sentences.en: if the labor has been done, the laborer is entitled to X.
sentences.zh: 如果劳动已经完成，劳动者就有权获得 X。

sentences.en: In a lot of our ancient Mesopotamian receipts, it's things like beer, and grain, and livestock.
sentences.zh: 在我们许多古代美索不达米亚的收据中，记录的东西包括啤酒、粮食和牲畜等。

sentences.en: And it's just unbelievably magical to see these materials, right?
sentences.zh: 看到这些材料，真是令人难以置信的神奇，对吧？

sentences.en: And then to imagine the system that created them and the systems that they supported.
sentences.zh: 然后想象创造它们的系统以及它们所支持的系统。

sentences.en: It's really quite an incredible thing to just put yourself back into that world, into a world that's so alien from the kind of system of market-based society that we live in today,
sentences.zh: 把自己重新带回那个世界，带回一个与我们今天生活的基于市场的社会系统如此格格不入的世界，这真是一件不可思议的事情，

sentences.en: and think about what it would be like to be that scribe, or to be the person who is, you know, asking the scribe to write this tablet,
sentences.zh: 去想想成为那个抄写员会是什么感觉，或者成为那个要求抄写员写这块泥板的人，

sentences.en: or to be, you know,
sentences.zh: 或者成为，你知道的，

sentences.en: the common person whose whole life is subjected to a kind of organization or production in a system of centralized administration based on these written records, based on writing.
sentences.zh: 那个普通人，他的一生都服从于某种组织或生产，置身于一个基于这些书面记录、基于书写的集权管理系统中。

sentences.en: This isn't a market the way that we traditionally understand markets, right?
sentences.zh: 这并不是我们传统理解的市场，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not sort of the idea that people come together in a place and exchange goods either by barter or by money.
sentences.zh: 这并不是那种人们聚集在一个地方通过以物易物或货币来交换货物的概念。

sentences.en: This is much more a kind of hierarchical system of organization to essentially allow for the creation of these larger-scale societies.
sentences.zh: 这更像是一种等级森严的组织系统，本质上是为了允许创建这种更大规模的社会。

sentences.en: So you've talked about this idea of centralized administration, and in some ways this brings us to another aspect of our story.
sentences.zh: 所以你谈到了这种集中管理的概念，在某种程度上，这把我们带到了我们故事的另一个方面。

sentences.en: We've talked a little bit about the idea of gift-giving and mutual obligations.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了送礼和相互义务的概念。

sentences.en: We've talked about the idea of receipts and record-keeping and essentially, you know, basic contracts that sort of bind us to one another over time.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了收据和记录保存的概念，以及本质上，你知道的，随着时间推移将我们彼此绑定的基本契约。

sentences.en: But talk also about this idea of the central administration of these systems and the introduction of what eventually become, you know,
sentences.zh: 但也要谈谈这些系统的中央管理的概念，以及最终成为，你知道的，

sentences.en: authorities that basically are overseeing how the whole system works.
sentences.zh: 监督整个系统如何运作的权威机构的引入。

sentences.en: So to make a money work, you need something that is both that system of reckoning and record-keeping, but also an authorizing power that says, in effect,
sentences.zh: 因此，要让货币发挥作用，你需要一种既是计算和记录系统，同时也是授权力量的东西，它实际上在说：

sentences.en: this is the way that we keep our records here.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们这里保存记录的方式。

sentences.en: So even in, you know, the highlands of New Guinea and then again in Mesopotamia, you've got both of those things going on, the system of record-keeping and the authorizing force.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在（你知道的）新几内亚高地，然后又在美索不达米亚，这两件事情都在发生：记录保存系统和授权力量。

sentences.en: And that's essentially what we have with modern money still today.
sentences.zh: 这本质上也就是我们今天现代化货币所拥有的东西。

sentences.en: We don't necessarily think of it that way.
sentences.zh: 我们不一定这样认为。

sentences.en: But basically, money is a unit of account that, in our case, is authorized by the state.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，货币是一个记账单位，在我们的例子中，它是得到国家授权的。

sentences.en: The state essentially sets the standard, and then that standard is used by people to reckon their relationships with one another, figure their debts and credits.
sentences.zh: 国家本质上设定了标准，然后人们使用这个标准来计算彼此之间的关系，弄清楚各自的债务和信用。

sentences.en: So the story that emerges about the origins of money is very different than the way we usually think about it.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于货币起源的故事与我们通常认为的非常不同。

sentences.en: In this model, embraced by Bill and other anthropologists, money is partly a mechanism of social obligation and partly a mechanism to keep track of who owes what to whom.
sentences.zh: 在这种被比尔和其他人类学家接受的模型中，货币一部分是社会义务的机制，一部分是追踪谁欠谁什么的机制。

sentences.en: It's also a mechanism that cements the relationship between ordinary people and authorities who maintain records.
sentences.zh: 它也是巩固普通人与维护记录的权威机构之间关系的机制。

sentences.en: In other words, it's a story about power.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是一个关于权力的故事。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: You've heard the old joke, nothing is certain except death and taxes.
sentences.zh: 你听过那句老笑话：世上除了死亡和税收，没有什么事是确定的。

sentences.en: Now, taxes may feel inevitable to us, but they were not always a part of human existence.
sentences.zh: 现在，税收对我们来说可能感觉是不可避免的，但它们并非一直都是人类存在的一部分。

sentences.en: Bill Morris says systems of taxation emerged as societies expanded and became more complex.
sentences.zh: 比尔·莫尔表示，随着社会扩张变得更加复杂，税收系统应运而生。

sentences.en: So in most of these systems, what you see is the development of something like a tax or a tribute or a tithe,
sentences.zh: 所以在大多数这类系统中，你会看到类似税收、贡品或什一税之类事物的出现

sentences.en: where a thing is sort of put out into the world.
sentences.zh: 也就是某种事物被投放到了世界上。

sentences.en: It can start off with just being, you know, grain or something like that.
sentences.zh: 它最初可能只是，你知道的，粮食或类似的东西。

sentences.en: But often what happened in ancient societies is rulers would take something that symbolized their own elite status,
sentences.zh: 但古代社会经常发生的情况是，统治者会拿走某种象征他们自身精英地位的东西，

sentences.en: usually precious metal, and send some of it out into the world and say,
sentences.zh: 通常是贵金属，然后把其中一部分送到世界上并说，

sentences.en: here, you know, you get this in exchange for serving in my army,
sentences.zh: 给你，你知道的，你得到这个是为了换取在我的军队里服役，

sentences.en: or you get this as a token to hold onto to remind you that you are subject to my rule.
sentences.zh: 或者你得到这个作为留作纪念的信物，提醒你你是受我统治的。

sentences.en: And in return, on some regular cycle every year, every seven years, you are expected to bring some of that back to me,
sentences.zh: 作为回报，在每年或每七年的某种定期循环中，你被期望把其中的一部分交还给我，

sentences.en: to demonstrate your fealty, to demonstrate your loyalty.
sentences.zh: 以证明你的效忠，证明你的忠诚。

sentences.en: And in effect, what we get is the origin of the first coins, things that look like coins to you and me,
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们得到的就是最初硬币的起源，那些对你我而言看起来像硬币的东西，

sentences.en: that are really serving as these kind of political tokens that express sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 它们真正起到的作用是表达主权的这种政治信物。

sentences.en: So I would get one of these things, and then I'm obligated at some point to, you know, get one of them or some of them back to you.
sentences.zh: 所以我得到了其中一件东西，然后我在某个时间点有义务，你知道的，把其中一件或几件还给你。

sentences.en: That instantly creates a market in these things.
sentences.zh: 这瞬间就在这些东西中创造了一个市场。

sentences.en: Everybody has to get their hands on these new tokens of political authority in order to give some back to the center.
sentences.zh: 每个人都必须弄到这些代表政治权力的行使新信物，以便向中心交回一部分。

sentences.en: So what's interesting is if I'm a king, and I'm basically saying, you not only need to pay me taxes,
sentences.zh: 所以有趣的是，如果我是一个国王，我基本上是在说，你不仅需要向我纳税，

sentences.en: but you need to pay me these taxes using my tokens, using my system of currency,
sentences.zh: 而且你还需要用我的信物，用我的货币体系来向我缴纳这些税，

sentences.en: the currency not only gains value because, of course, people are now trading the currency and doing things with it and involving transactions,
sentences.zh: 这种货币不仅获得了价值，因为当然，人们现在正在交易这种货币并用它做事情以及参与交易，

sentences.en: but it also sort of binds them to me and establishes my power over them,
sentences.zh: 而且它也某种程度上把他们绑定在我身上，确立了我对他们的权力，

sentences.en: because I'm basically saying this is the language in which transactions can take place, and that's extraordinarily powerful.
sentences.zh: 因为我基本上是在说，这是交易得以进行的语言，而那是极其强大的。

sentences.en: It's unbelievably powerful, and it's sort of the invisible power of the king in that sense.
sentences.zh: 这是难以置信的强大，从某种意义上说，这就是国王无形的力量。

sentences.en: You can see this invisible power of the state each year when it comes time to file out tax returns.
sentences.zh: 每年到了填写纳税申报表的时候，你就能看到国家这种无形的力量。

sentences.en: In the United States, citizens are obliged not only to pay taxes, but also to figure out how much they owe.
sentences.zh: 在美国，公民不仅有义务纳税，还有义务计算出他们欠多少税。

sentences.en: Here's a skit from the social media platform TikTok about this idea.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个关于这个想法的来自社交媒体平台TikTok的小品。

sentences.en: Yeah, so you actually owe us money.
sentences.zh: 对，所以你实际上欠我们钱。

sentences.en: It's called taxes.
sentences.zh: 这叫税。

sentences.en: Okay, how much money do I owe you guys?
sentences.zh: 好的，我欠你们多少钱？

sentences.en: Actually, you have to figure that out.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你必须自己算出来。

sentences.en: Okay, so I can just, like, pay whatever I want.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我就可以，比如，我想付多少就付多少。

sentences.en: Well, not exactly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不完全是这样。

sentences.en: Like, we know, like, the exact number of how much you owe, but you also have to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们知道，比如，你欠多少钱的确切数字，但你也必须把它算出来。

sentences.en: Well, what if I mess up and get the number wrong?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果我搞砸了，数字算错了会怎么样？

sentences.en: You owe you to prison.
sentences.zh: 你会被判入狱。

sentences.en: That's hilarious.
sentences.zh: 这太滑稽了。

sentences.en: So talk about this idea, Bill, which is, in some ways, this is how many Americans feel about their taxes.
sentences.zh: 所以聊聊这个想法吧，比尔，从某些方面来说，这就是许多美国人对他们税收的感受。

sentences.en: What does this tell us, in some ways, about the nature of money, power, and the state?
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来说，这向我们揭示了关于金钱、权力和国家的本质的什么信息？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, you know, it's sort of right out there, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对，嗯，你知道的，它就摆在那里，不是吗？

sentences.en: That, you know, it's sort of on you to report your income, and if you do it wrong or, you know, don't quite get it right,
sentences.zh: 就是，你知道的，申报你的收入主要靠你自己，如果你做错了，或者，你知道的，没完全弄对，

sentences.en: we're going to come after you through an audit or something.
sentences.zh: 我们就会通过审计或其他方式来找你算账。

sentences.en: It really does kind of elevate the power of the state above us mere mortals.
sentences.zh: 它确实把国家的力量提升到了我们这些凡人之上。

sentences.en: And, again, represents, you know, the authority the state has, both in terms of the standard of account, our money, and in terms of daily affairs having to do with that money.
sentences.zh: 而且，再次体现了，你知道的，国家所拥有的权威，无论是在记账标准、我们的钱方面，还是在与该钱有关的日常事务方面。

sentences.en: So one of the interesting things to consider here is that there might be actually different competing ideas about the nature and origin of money.
sentences.zh: 所以这里需要考虑的有趣事情之一是，关于金钱的本质和起源，实际上可能存在着不同的、相互竞争的观点。

sentences.en: You know, one of them says it's transactional, it's functional.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中一种观点认为它是交易性的，它是功能性的。

sentences.en: This is sort of what you learn in Economics 101.
sentences.zh: 这有点像你在《经济学101》里学到的东西。

sentences.en: The model that you're painting is that this is much more about relationships and mutual obligations and histories of those obligations
sentences.zh: 你所描绘的模式是，这更多地关乎关系、相互义务以及这些义务的历史，

sentences.en: and how those are recorded and preserved over time and the state authorities that might be involved in preserving them and their relationship to you and so forth.
sentences.zh: 以及这些义务是如何随着时间的推移而被记录和保存的，还有可能参与其中的国家权力以及他们与你的关系等等。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you could talk a little bit about what happened when these different systems, if you will, clashed with one another.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否能谈谈，当这些不同的体系（如果你愿意这么叫的话）互相发生冲突时会发生什么。

sentences.en: You've talked about how when European colonists went to Africa and Asia, in some ways they encountered different systems than the ones they were used to.
sentences.zh: 你谈到过，当欧洲殖民者前往非洲和亚洲时，他们在某些方面遇到了与他们习惯的不同体系。

sentences.en: And in some ways you had not just a clash of people and a clash of civilizations, if you will, but a clash of how you define what money actually is during these encounters.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，在这些相遇中，你不仅面临着人与人的冲突、文明的冲突（如果你愿意的话），还面临着对金钱到底是什么的定义的冲突。

sentences.en: Yeah, Europeans consistently misidentified things like shells or metal rods or bracelets and things like that around the world as the kind of money that they were used to.
sentences.zh: 是的，欧洲人一直把世界各地诸如贝壳、金属棒或手镯之类东西误识别为他们所习惯的那种金钱。

sentences.en: And so what would they do?
sentences.zh: 那他们会怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Well, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，

sentences.en: one thing that they would do is they would forcibly introduce their own standard as kind of typical means of colonization and subjugation in sub-Saharan Africa was to demand that colonized people pay taxes in European money,
sentences.zh: 他们会做的一件事就是强行引入他们自己的标准，作为撒哈拉以南非洲殖民和征服的一种典型手段，即要求被殖民的人用欧洲货币纳税，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: That then meant that they had to get that European money,
sentences.zh: 那这就意味着他们必须弄到那种欧洲货币，

sentences.en: which meant that they would have to do things like grow crops or sell things or engage in the slave trade or something like that that would generate that money they could give back.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们将不得不做一些事情，比如种植庄稼、出售东西、参与奴隶贸易或类似的事情，从而产生他们可以交还的货币。

sentences.en: Or in other cases, European powers would just reset the standard by saying, you know, these shells before were good,
sentences.zh: 或者在其他情况下，欧洲列强会通过以下方式重置标准，你知道的，以前这些贝壳很好，

sentences.en: but this other shell is better and we're going to demand our taxes in this other shell.
sentences.zh: 但这个别的贝壳更好，我们将要求用这个别的贝壳纳税。

sentences.en: Again, similarly setting up a market in these other shells, which then completely contorted the societies that were subject to colonial rule.
sentences.zh: 同样地，在这些其他贝壳中建立了一个市场，这彻底扭曲了受殖民统治支配的社会。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有趣。

sentences.en: Money in some ways was a tool of colonization.
sentences.zh: 金钱在某种程度上是殖民主义的工具。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I think money has always been a tool of political authority.
sentences.zh: 我认为金钱一直都是政治权力的工具。

sentences.en: Bill says political authority is drawn not just from issuing money, but from the act of designing it.
sentences.zh: 比尔说，政治权力不仅来源于发行货币，还来源于设计货币的行为。

sentences.en: The images you see on a bill or a coin can say a great deal about a nation's values and aspirations.
sentences.zh: 你在钞票或硬币上看到的图案可以很大程度上说明一个国家的价值观和抱负。

sentences.en: In 2015, the Treasury Secretary invited Bill and other scholars to Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 2015年，财政部长邀请比尔和其他学者前往华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: They were to discuss a proposed redesign of the $10 bill.
sentences.zh: 他们要讨论重新设计10美元纸币的提案。

sentences.en: I was invited to come and just have a kind of brainstorming session about what could be done, what sorts of figures would be appropriate,
sentences.zh: 我被邀请去参加一个头脑风暴会议，讨论可以做些什么，什么样的形象是合适的，

sentences.en: what sorts of iconography would be appropriate for the new banknote.
sentences.zh: 什么样的符号对于这枚新纸币是合适的。

sentences.en: And it really was like a kind of graduate seminar.
sentences.zh: 这真的就像一个研究生研讨会。

sentences.en: We just kind of had a wide-ranging conversation about women's history in the United States, about the history of slavery and emancipation and the civil rights movement,
sentences.zh: 我们只是进行了一场广泛的对话，关于美国女性的历史，关于奴隶制和解放的历史以及民权运动，

sentences.en: and about the kinds of things that you could do on a banknote,
sentences.zh: 以及你可以在钞票上做的事情的种类，

sentences.en: the kinds of stories that you could tell on the money about the nation and the ways those stories could make people feel included in the nation in a new way.
sentences.zh: 你可以在钱上讲述的关于这个国家的故事的种类，以及这些故事能让人们以一种全新的方式感受到自己被这个国家包容的方式。

sentences.en: Again, this was happening in 2015.
sentences.zh: 再次说明，这是在2015年发生的。

sentences.en: That was the same year that the musical Hamilton debuted on Broadway.
sentences.zh: 那也是音乐剧《汉密尔顿》在百老汇首演的同一年。

sentences.en: His financial system is a work of genius.
sentences.zh: 他的金融体系是天才之作。

sentences.en: I couldn't undo it if I tried.
sentences.zh: 就算我想撤销我也做不到。

sentences.en: And it reminded everyone of the role that Alexander Hamilton played in establishing our banking system.
sentences.zh: 这提醒了每个人亚历山大·汉密尔顿在建立我们的银行体系中发挥的作用。

sentences.en: The figure on the 10 currently is Alexander Hamilton, and we thought maybe we want to keep him.
sentences.zh: 目前10美元上的人物是亚历山大·汉密尔顿，我们觉得也许我们想留着他。

sentences.en: So Bill and the group decide that instead of redesigning the $10 bill, they should update the 20.
sentences.zh: 所以比尔和这个小组决定，与其重新设计10美元纸币，不如更新20美元纸币。

sentences.en: Since the 20 is a more ubiquitous banknote, it's the one that comes out of all the ATMs, it's much more common in people's daily transactions than the 10.
sentences.zh: 由于20美元是一张更无处不在的纸币，它是所有自动取款机里吐出来的钱，在人们的日常交易中比10美元要常见得多。

sentences.en: The image of Andrew Jackson, the seventh president of the United States, has been on the $20 bill since 1928.
sentences.zh: 美国第七任总统安德鲁·杰克逊的肖像自1928年以来一直印在20美元纸币上。

sentences.en: Jackson's tenure was marked by the signing of the Indian Removal Act, which resulted in the deaths of thousands of indigenous people.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊的任期以签署《印第安人迁移法案》为标志，该法案导致了成千上万原住民的死亡。

sentences.en: Bill and other members of the group in Washington felt a woman should take Jackson's place.
sentences.zh: 比尔和华盛顿小组的其他成员认为，应该由一位女性来取代杰克逊的位置。

sentences.en: They gravitated toward a hero of the Underground Railroad.
sentences.zh: 他们倾向于地下铁路的一位女英雄。

sentences.en: There was really strong consensus around Harriet Tubman, in part because having her on the bill would help to sort of, you know,
sentences.zh: 围绕哈莉特·塔布曼存在着非常强烈的共识，部分原因是因为让她登上钞票将有助于，你知道的，

sentences.en: sketch and then complete a story arc about American society, about increasing the franchise, about emancipation, about the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 勾勒并完成一个关于美国社会的宏大叙事，关于扩大选举权，关于解放，关于民权运动。

sentences.en: And one of the things that got all of us very excited was when the then treasurer of the United States, Rosie Rios, passed around her favorite banknote, which is the $2 bill.
sentences.zh: 让我们所有人都感到非常兴奋的事情之一是，时任美国财政部长罗西·里奥斯传阅了她最喜欢的纸币，也就是2美元纸币。

sentences.en: And she passed it around for us to look at.
sentences.zh: 她把它传阅开来让我们看。

sentences.en: And she's like, take a look at the back.
sentences.zh: 然后她说，看一看背面。

sentences.en: We look at the back.
sentences.zh: 我们看了背面。

sentences.en: Unlike all of the other American banknotes, the $2 bill has a scene.
sentences.zh: 与所有其他美国纸币不同，2美元纸币有一个场景。

sentences.en: It has people standing together signing the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 它有人们站在一起签署《独立宣言》的画面。

sentences.en: And she said, you know, what can you do if you activate the back of the note with people?
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道的，如果你用人物来激活纸币的背面，你能做到什么？

sentences.en: And then, you know, our minds kind of went racing around that idea of, you know, you could have the $5 bill, keep Lincoln on the front, keep the Lincoln Memorial on the back,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，我们的思绪开始围绕着那个想法飞转，你知道的，你可以有5美元纸币，正面保留林肯，背面保留林肯纪念堂，

sentences.en: but populate it with the Civil Rights March and a tiny little Martin Luther King giving his I Have a Dream speech or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但在上面填满民权游行的场景，再加上一个发表《我有一个梦想》演讲的微小马丁·路德·金或类似的东西。

sentences.en: There was a point where I think we got a little too excited and too creative.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，我认为我们变得有点过于兴奋和有创造力了。

sentences.en: And the treasurer said, you know, bear in mind, there's a limited amount of real estate on this thing.
sentences.zh: 财政部长说，你知道的，请记住，这东西上的空间是有限的。

sentences.en: And there's only so much that designers can do.
sentences.zh: 设计师能做的事情是有限的。

sentences.en: And don't forget that all of the counterfeit detection stuff has to go in there, too.
sentences.zh: 别忘了所有的防伪技术也都必须塞进去。

sentences.en: Too creative.

sentences.en: But that's kind of really where our minds went,
sentences.zh: 但那确实是我们的思绪所到的地方，

sentences.en: because we started thinking about all of the stories that you can tell on this thing that really is still one of the most ubiquitous forms of mass media in the United States.
sentences.zh: 因为我们开始思考所有你可以在这个东西上讲述的故事，它实际上仍然是美国最普遍的大众传媒形式之一。

sentences.en: The announcement about the $20 bill redesign was made in April 2016.
sentences.zh: 关于重新设计20美元纸币的公告是在2016年4月发布的。

sentences.en: Harriet Tubman, who helped more than 300 slaves find freedom through the Underground Railroad, will be the new face of the $20 bill.
sentences.zh: 哈莉特·塔布曼通过地下铁路帮助了300多名奴隶重获自由，她将成为20美元纸币的新面孔。

sentences.en: Tubman will be the first woman featured on the front of U.S.
sentences.zh: 塔布曼将成为第一位出现在美国货币正面的女性。

sentences.en: currency.
sentences.zh: 货币。

sentences.en: Andrew Jackson would remain on one side of the bill, and Harriet Tubman would be on the other.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·杰克逊将留在纸币的一侧，而哈莉特·塔布曼将在另一侧。

sentences.en: The rebranding was announced during President Barack Obama's final year in office.
sentences.zh: 这项品牌重塑是在贝拉克·奥巴马总统任期的最后一年宣布的。

sentences.en: Then-presidential candidate Donald Trump called the decision pure political correctness.
sentences.zh: 时任总统候选人唐纳德·特朗普称这一决定纯粹是政治正确。

sentences.en: He was asked about the redesign on NBC's Today Show.
sentences.zh: 他在NBC的《今日秀》节目中被问及重新设计的事。

sentences.en: I think Harriet Tubman is fantastic.
sentences.zh: 我认为哈莉特·塔布曼太棒了。

sentences.en: I would love to leave Andrew Jackson and see if we can maybe come up with another denomination.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意保留安德鲁·杰克逊，看看我们是否能想出另一个面额。

sentences.en: Maybe we do the $2 bill.
sentences.zh: 也许我们用2美元纸币。

sentences.en: Less than a year after the redesign was announced, Donald Trump became president.
sentences.zh: 在宣布重新设计不到一年后，唐纳德·特朗普当选总统。

sentences.en: In the Oval Office, he hung a portrait of his favorite predecessor.
sentences.zh: 在椭圆形办公室里，他悬挂了他最喜欢的前任的画像。

sentences.en: It was Andrew Jackson.
sentences.zh: 那就是安德鲁·杰克逊。

sentences.en: And in the summer of 2019...
sentences.zh: 而在2019年夏天……

sentences.en: Andrew Jackson is keeping his place on the $20 bill for now.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·杰克逊目前将继续保留他在20美元纸币上的位置。

sentences.en: That's according to Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin, whose department oversees the design of currency.
sentences.zh: 这是根据财政部长史蒂芬·姆努钦的说法，他的部门负责监管货币的设计。

sentences.en: The Trump administration tabled the redesign just months before the bill was expected to be released.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府在预计发行该纸币的前几个月搁置了重新设计的计划。

sentences.en: The ultimate decision on the redesign will most likely be another secretary's down the road.
sentences.zh: 对重新设计的最终决定很可能是未来另一位财政部长的职责。

sentences.en: So it seems like the project is on hold right now, and we'll see how things develop.
sentences.zh: 所以这个项目现在似乎处于搁置状态，我们要看看事情会如何发展。

sentences.en: Regardless, the notes will have to be redesigned because of the overriding reason for which they're redesigned, which is anti-counterfeiting.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这些纸币都必须重新设计，因为重新设计的首要原因，那就是反假冒。

sentences.en: So we'll see what happens.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: More recently, the Biden administration has restarted the plan to put Harriet Tubman on the $20 bill.
sentences.zh: 最近，拜登政府重新启动了将哈莉特·塔布曼印上20美元纸币的计划。

sentences.en: It's reportedly slated to be released in 2030.
sentences.zh: 据报道，它定于2030年发行。

sentences.en: The faces and scenes we see on our money communicate our values as a nation.
sentences.zh: 我们在金钱上看到的面孔和场景传达了我们作为一个国家的价值观。

sentences.en: And the way we use that money communicates something about us as individuals.
sentences.zh: 我们使用金钱的方式传达了我们作为个体的某些特质。

sentences.en: When I give you money, I'm not just giving you a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 当我给你钱时，我不只是给你一张纸。

sentences.en: I'm giving you my word, my bond.
sentences.zh: 我给你的是我的诺言，我的契约。

sentences.en: Society is a thing of ongoing, continuous relationships and unsettled debts, right?
sentences.zh: 社会是一个持续不断的、连续的关系和未了债务的事物，对吧？

sentences.en: Some years ago, the economist Joel Wolfogel wrote a paper.
sentences.zh: 几年前，经济学家乔尔·沃尔福格尔写了一篇论文。

sentences.en: It was titled The Deadweight Loss of Christmas.
sentences.zh: 它的标题是《圣诞节的无谓损失》。

sentences.en: He argued that it made no sense for me to give you gifts that you don't like,
sentences.zh: 他认为，我送你你不喜欢的礼物，你送我我不喜欢的礼物，这毫无意义。

sentences.en: and for you to give me gifts that I don't like.
sentences.zh: 我送你你不喜欢的礼物，你送我我不喜欢的礼物，这毫无意义。

sentences.en: We would both be better off keeping our money and spending it on the things we do like.
sentences.zh: 我们俩留着自己的钱并把它花在我们真正喜欢的东西上会更好。

sentences.en: Anthropologist Bill Morrow has many disputes with how economists see the world of money.
sentences.zh: 人类学家比尔·莫罗对经济学家看待金钱世界的方式有许多异议。

sentences.en: Joel Wolfogel's argument might be ground zero.
sentences.zh: 乔尔·沃尔福格尔的论点可能是这一切的原点。

sentences.en: I think one of the things that economists are always imagining is that the end of transactions
sentences.zh: 我认为经济学家总是想象的一件事是，交易的目的

sentences.en: is to have them settled, right?
sentences.zh: 是让它们了结，对吧？

sentences.en: That we enter a relationship of debt, and then we want to settle that debt.
sentences.zh: 我们进入了一种债务关系，然后我们想要了结那笔债务。

sentences.en: So you hand me over something at the store, and I give you money at the till, and then it's over,
sentences.zh: 所以你在店里递给我一样东西，我在收银台给你钱，然后就结束了，

sentences.en: and then we go our separate ways.
sentences.zh: 然后我们各奔东西。

sentences.en: They love that kind of vision of the frictionless market where parties come to the market anonymously,
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢那种无摩擦市场的愿景，各方在其中匿名交易，

sentences.en: and money is the thing that mediates their relationship,
sentences.zh: 金钱在他们之间起着中介作用，

sentences.en: so that then they continue to go on anonymously.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以继续保持匿名状态。

sentences.en: The problem is that if you imagine a world where all debts are settled, then what is that world?
sentences.zh: 问题是，如果你想象一个所有债务都已清偿的世界，那会是一个怎样的世界？

sentences.en: That's a world then of no more relationships, of no more mutuality, of no more obligation.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个没有更多关系、没有更多互惠、没有更多义务的世界。

sentences.en: Society is not a society of settled debts.
sentences.zh: 社会并非一个债务两清的社会。

sentences.en: Society is a thing of ongoing continuous relationships and unsettled debts, right?
sentences.zh: 社会是由不断持续的关系和未偿清的债务构成的，对吧？

sentences.en: The settling and unsettling of debts on and on and on and on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 债务不断地、不断地、不断地被清偿又未清偿。

sentences.en: There's no moment where it ends, or at least if there was a moment where it ended,
sentences.zh: 没有哪个时刻是终结的，或者说，即使真有一个终结的时刻，

sentences.en: we'd all just be alone in bunkers, hiding, doing nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们也只会独自躲在掩体里，无所事事。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering if this is connected to some very interesting phenomena that we see,
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，这是否与我们所看到的一些非常有趣的现象有关，

sentences.en: which is that even after coming up with this remarkable invention, money,
sentences.zh: 那就是，即使在发明了金钱这个了不起的工具之后，

sentences.en: we've also come up with lots of ways to make money inefficient and difficult to use.
sentences.zh: 我们又想出了许许多多方法，让金钱变得效率低下且难以使用。

sentences.en: So we give our friends gift cards to restaurants that limit, in some ways, how they can use the money.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们送给朋友餐馆的礼品卡，在某种程度上限制了他们使用这笔钱的方式。

sentences.en: In some ways, it would be easier just to give them cash,
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，直接给他们现金会更简单，

sentences.en: and they could use it at the restaurant or not use it at the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 他们既可以在那家餐馆使用，也可以不用。

sentences.en: What do these inefficient forms of money tell us about the role that money plays in personal relationships?
sentences.zh: 这些低效的货币形式向我们传达了关于金钱在人际关系中扮演什么角色的信息？

sentences.en: Yeah, I love this kind of stuff because it really shows you that money is never purely fungible, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我非常喜欢这类事情，因为它真正向你展示了金钱从来都不是纯粹同质的，对吧？

sentences.en: We're continuously putting boundaries around different pots of money,
sentences.zh: 我们不断在不同的资金池周围划定界限，

sentences.en: and those boundaries are often moral boundaries.
sentences.zh: 而这些界限往往是道德界限。

sentences.en: They signify a moral or ethical or relational stance that we want to take with respect to one another.
sentences.zh: 它们象征着我们希望在彼此关系中采取的某种道德、伦理或关系的立场。

sentences.en: And this kind of earmarking of money for special purposes,
sentences.zh: 而这种为特殊目的给金钱贴标签的行为，

sentences.en: this kind of sequestering of some money, taking it out of circulation
sentences.zh: 这种将部分资金隔离、使其脱离流通的做法，

sentences.en: and keeping it in a special place for only a special purpose,
sentences.zh: 并将其保存在一个特殊地方仅用于特殊目的，

sentences.en: really does help us make the stuff of social life,
sentences.zh: 确实有助于我们构建社会生活的实质，

sentences.en: helps us stitch ourselves together and bind us to one another
sentences.zh: 帮助我们把彼此缝合在一起、紧密相连，

sentences.en: in ways that far exceed the imagination of money as just a neutral medium of exchange.
sentences.zh: 其程度远远超出了将金钱仅视为中性交换媒介的想象。

sentences.en: The tensions between these two models of money,
sentences.zh: 这两种货币模型之间的紧张关系，

sentences.en: between the economist model and the anthropologist model,
sentences.zh: 即经济学家模型与人类学家模型之间的紧张关系，

sentences.en: exist within each of us.
sentences.zh: 存在于我们每个人心中。

sentences.en: We couldn't function as economic actors
sentences.zh: 如果没有把金钱视为中性匿名交换形式的能力，

sentences.en: without the capacity to think of money as a neutral form of anonymous exchange.
sentences.zh: 我们就无法作为经济行动者运转。

sentences.en: Of course, all of us also intuitively understand how debts and obligations work,
sentences.zh: 当然，我们所有人都凭直觉理解债务和义务是如何运作的，

sentences.en: and we sometimes become uncomfortable
sentences.zh: 有时当这两种模型发生冲突时，

sentences.en: when these two models collide with one another.
sentences.zh: 我们会感到不自在。

sentences.en: For example, we have struggled for decades
sentences.zh: 例如，几十年来我们一直在与那些耗时且困难的活动带来的挑战作斗争，

sentences.en: with the challenge of time-consuming and difficult activities
sentences.zh: 比如育儿、家务劳动或照顾年迈的父母。

sentences.en: like parenting or domestic work or caring for aging parents.
sentences.zh: 我们应该把这些事情当作工作来看待吗？

sentences.en: Should we think of these things as jobs?
sentences.zh: 给它们标上美元价格吗？

sentences.en: Put a dollar figure on them?
sentences.zh: 还是说某些事情应该存在于金钱领域之外？

sentences.en: Or should some things exist outside the sphere of money?
sentences.zh: 这是当代西方社会现代主体的一种悖论，

sentences.en: This is kind of a paradox of modern subjects in contemporary Western societies,
sentences.zh: 那就是我们首先认为自己是独立的个体，

sentences.en: is that we think of ourselves as individuals first
sentences.zh: 其次才是关系的成员，

sentences.en: and members of relationships second,
sentences.zh: 尽管当然，我们只有通过关系才能塑造自我，对吧？

sentences.en: even though, of course, it's only through relationships that we get formed, right?
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为我父母之间的关系，我就不会存在，

sentences.en: I wouldn't exist if it were not for a relationship between my parents,
sentences.zh: 如果周围没有一个群体网络，

sentences.en: and I wouldn't be able to be speaking to you now
sentences.zh: 教我语言，对吧？

sentences.en: if there weren't a network of folks around me
sentences.zh: 教我如何在这个世界生存，

sentences.en: who taught me language, right?
sentences.zh: 以及如何成为一个建立联系的人，

sentences.en: and how to be a person that makes connections.
sentences.zh: 然而，由于我们有着这样一种意识形态，

sentences.en: And yet, because we have this kind of ideology
sentences.zh: 即我们每个人都是一个全新的人，

sentences.en: that we are each a new person,
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都独立存在，

sentences.en: we are our own autonomous agent,

sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否跟我多讲讲，

sentences.zh: 到最后，我们基本上每天都在彼此家里吃饭，

sentences.zh: 所以我们想，你知道的，

sentences.en: So we thought, you know,

sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，有时你做出这些决定时，

sentences.zh: 如果我退一步看看自己的情况，

sentences.en: and economic relationships,
sentences.zh: 这其实挺有趣的，

sentences.en: if I take a step back and look at my own situation,
